chapter: Reel 2: touring, shows and the war
title: Benny Carter: leaving New York
summary: Scott says he never worked with Carter, who was disconsolate before going to California.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: No, somewhere during that period, didn't you go with Benny ?

No, I knew Benny, but I didn't work with him,no. See, I was working at the time. I knew Benny, I remember one time when I was coming from the Amsterdam or something. And Gene and I, we were walking down the avenue and we met Benny. And he seemed kind of disconsolate. I asked him what was the matter, and he said, oh, Scottie, I'm kind of disgusted, I'm going to leave New York.

And there he is, a good saxophone player like he was. I said, what, leave? Why, Benny? He says, I don't know, it looks like I just can't get anywhere and all like that. I don't know, and he'd been playing and writing and making records and things. So we were going down to an opening, Jack Fuller was opening up his place, at the old Colony, and he was opening that night. And we were going by there, and I say, come

on with us, Benny. We took him down there, and we sat there, the three of us. And we had a couple of drinks. And I tried to convince him, but his mind was made up. He says, I'm going out to California.
(Inaudible.) And it listed you as being in the band, and they raised the question, they wanted to know if Benny Carter was stealing the Henderson band. You don't remember anything about that?

No, well, see, that was after I left Fletcher. That was after I left Fletcher. But, see, I went straight with Duke, then. And I didn't go with Bennie, no. Bennie didn't make good with bands here. But he went out to Chicago -- California, out there, and tore up California. He made gangs of records out there. They had bands out there -- there's nothing but Benny Carter out there now.
